questions.question: Which package manager / build tool should be used, and what exact command installs dependencies?
questions.truth: Go modules (go.mod). `make install_deps` runs `go get -v ./...`; `go mod download` is the plain equivalent. `go test` also fetches automatically.
accept: saying no separate install step is needed because go build/test fetches modules

questions.question: What exact command runs the full test suite?
questions.truth: `make test` (install_deps then `go test -v ./...`); CI runs `make richtest` (richgo wrapper of the same). Plain: `go test ./...`.

questions.question: What exact command runs only the tests in doc/md_docs_test.go?
questions.truth: Go cannot select tests by file. The tests in doc/md_docs_test.go are TestGenMdDoc, TestGenMdDocWithNoLongOrSynopsis, TestGenMdNoHiddenParents, TestGenMdNoTag, TestGenMdTree, all in package ./doc: `go test ./doc -run 'TestGenMd'` (or naming them).
accept: go test ./doc -run <regex matching/naming the TestGenMd* functions> (e.g. -run TestGenMd or the five names)
reject: go test ./doc alone = 0.5 (also runs tests from the other doc test files)
go test doc/md_docs_test.go = 0 (fails: helpers live in other files)
go test ./... -run X where X is not from that file

questions.question: What exact command(s) check lint/formatting the way CI does?
questions.truth: CI: golangci-lint run (config .golangci.yml enables gofmt/goimports formatters + linters) via golangci-lint-action; also an addlicense -check for license headers. Local: `make lint` (golangci-lint run -v) and `make fmt` (gofmt -l check).
accept: make lint / golangci-lint run (make fmt / gofmt -l an optional extra; addlicense a bonus)
reject: golint / standalone staticcheck as the CI check

questions.question: Name files or directories in this repo that are generated or vendored and must not be edited by hand (or say none).
questions.truth: None. No committed generated or vendored code (no vendor/ dir, no DO NOT EDIT files besides tool-maintained go.sum).
reject: claiming doc/, site/ or assets/ are generated or vendored
